svg.aria-label: Anatomy of the gate: flow queues, the saturation score, running slots and the waiting queue
svg.text: What the gate reads, and what a slot is
Flow control lives in the endpoint picker. Slots and the waiting queue live in vLLM. The gate is the endpoint picker reading vLLM and deciding whether to release more work.
ENDPOINT PICKER
Tenant A
Tenant B
Tenant C
one queue per tenant, per priority
gate
open or
closed
vLLM
Running slots, max_num_seqs 128
Waiting queue, vllm:num_requests_waiting
26 dispatched, not yet in a slot
→ output
A slot is one request, not one token
max_num_seqs caps how many requests vLLM runs at
once. A request holds its slot from prefill until
its last token. Every decode step advances all 128
sequences, so a fuller batch makes every token
slower for everyone in it.
The waiting queue is downstream of the gate
These requests were already released by the endpoint
picker. They are waiting for a slot to free. This is
the number the gate reads back, which is why the
gate is reactive rather than predictive.
Queue depth threshold is a flow control setting
It configures the endpoint picker, not vLLM. The
score is waiting divided by threshold, against KV
used divided by the KV limit, whichever is larger,
averaged across pods. At 1.0 the gate closes. With
one pod there is nothing to average, so that pod is
the pool.
Threshold 1 trips the gate on the first waiting request. Threshold 4 tolerates four. Neither one is a cap on how long the waiting queue may grow.
